profile.name: Jake Kim
profile.headline: I build financial software people trust with real money.
intro: An AI-native product engineer who started in crypto and has built dApps, on-chain games, and an institutional trading terminal.

Right now I'm building OrderX, a multi-exchange crypto derivatives terminal. I use Claude and Codex as planner and reviewer, run the systems I design all the way to production, and like building big products with small teams.

experiences.oneLiner: A [[multi-exchange]] terminal built toward an institutional [[trading-desk]]. $10B [[notional]] processed and $1M revenue during pilot and private beta.
bullets: Designed the order-execution flow that bundles [[options]] and futures orders across venues and accounts into one [[order-form]], unifying each exchange's symbol format and account structure on the frontend.

Cut steady-state browser memory from 3.8GB to about 1GB. Replaced [[react-grid-layout]]'s CPU-bound layout math with a [[translate-grid|translate-based grid]] so chart-heavy dashboards drag without stutter.

Established a [[context-injection]] + Claude–Codex [[planner-reviewer]] workflow. Edge cases that a single model or agent would have left to resurface days or weeks later get caught at review, saving one to three-plus working days per feature. Built a [[figma-mcp|Figma MCP]] + [[i18n]] agent pipeline for localization.

detail.description: A terminal that starts from crypto [[derivatives]] and is heading toward an institutional [[trading-desk]]. It handles crypto venues (Deribit, Hyperliquid, Lighter, Bybit, Binance) and traditional markets (OPRA US options, CME, IBKR) on one screen. Piloted with a large [[multistrat|multistrat fund]]; $10B [[notional]] processed and $1M in revenue during private beta. I built the frontend from initial setup as the sole owner, pairing on the harder stretches, and designed its 18 feature domains.
impact: $10B [[notional]] processed and $1M revenue during pilot and private beta. Pilot run with a large [[multistrat|multistrat fund]].
Unified order execution and [[multi-exchange]] support on the frontend, so traders place orders across accounts from one screen instead of hopping between exchanges.
Steady-state browser memory from 3.8GB down to about 1GB, so an all-day trading session no longer needs reloads.

AI workflow: edge cases that single-agent work used to leave behind are caught at the planner/reviewer stage, saving one to three-plus working days per feature. A small team finished the entire MVP flow. Localization automated through a Figma to i18n-agent pipeline.

projects.title: Order execution and multi-exchange support
projects.problem: Traders hold several accounts across venues like Deribit, Hyperliquid, and Bybit, and the same BTC option has a different symbol, decimals, and margin model on each. They used to hop between exchange screens to trade, and a slip sent money to the wrong account or instrument.
approach: One [[order-form]] that selects several instruments and submits them together as a [[batch-order]]. Each leg gets an [[anchor-price]] so the preview shows an expected fill, and nothing leaves without passing validation.
An [[account-resolution]] rule that combines instrument, venue, and the user's choice to pick the destination account automatically, blocking wrong-account mistakes in the UI.

Venue symbol formats (Deribit 'BTC-26DEC25-90000-C' vs OPRA 'IBIT_271217P00048000') handled as structured fields (underlying, expiry, strike, call/put) rather than strings, so adding a venue does not break order logic.

Professional order types layered on top: [[tp-sl|TP/SL]] brackets, [[rfq|RFQ]] quotes, [[spreader|Spreader]] matrix orders, [[arb|Arb builder]], [[hedge|Hedge]] simulation, [[twap|TWAP]] slicing, [[one-tap|One-tap buy]].

Found that the [[uicontext|UIContext]] passed to the AI for chat orders could not express [[batch-order|batch orders]] or [[tp-sl|TP/SL]], wrote the fix as an [[rfc|RFC]], and changed the protocol with the backend team. Proposed '@account' tags to route each instrument to its own account.
Showed that merging positions from several accounts into one table is unsafe because server messages carry no account identifier, and documented it as a backend change request.

projects.title: Browser memory optimization (3.8GB → 1GB)
projects.problem: Real-time streams, widget state, TradingView iframes, and query caches accumulated until Chrome sat at 3.8GB, slowing the UI and eventually killing the tab.
approach: Split [[orderbook]] and [[position-table|position table]] updates down to row and symbol granularity to remove redundant re-renders and allocations.
Replaced AG Grid with an in-house DataTable with row memoization, virtualization, and clean unsubscribe paths.
Three-stage [[runtime-recovery]]: partial resubscribe, then cache invalidation, then reload when returning from a background tab. Reloads are blocked while an order is being entered.

projects.title: Translate-based in-house grid system
projects.problem: [[react-grid-layout]] recalculated layout and re-rendered React on every mousemove during resize, saturating the CPU.
approach: dnd-kit plus imperative DOM transform ([[translate-grid|translate]]) updates so React is out of the loop while dragging.
Grid-to-pixel math isolated in pure functions and pinned with tests.
Widget stretch and shareable page layouts with auto-generated OG images.

projects.title: AI workflow adoption
projects.problem: A small team had to push MVP features across 18 domains at once. Single-model, single-agent work shipped fine on day one but left edge cases behind, so the same feature had to be reopened days or weeks later.
approach: Repository conventions, architecture, and domain rules fixed through [[context-injection]] so any agent works to the same standard.
Claude as planner, Codex as reviewer ([[planner-reviewer]]): design, implementation, and review separated, with plan/design documents and gap analysis as the audit trail.
[[react-doctor]] cleanups run as a routine so debt from feature integration does not accumulate.
Outcome: coverage over speed. Edge cases caught at review removed one to three-plus working days of rework per feature.

projects.title: Figma MCP + i18n agent pipeline
projects.problem: Design changes and translated copy were applied by hand, so every release shipped with omissions and mismatches.
approach: [[figma-mcp|Figma MCP]] reads the design source directly to apply component changes.
An [[i18n]] agent finds missing keys, translates and registers them, and syncs with Lokalise. Localization runs on next-intl.

projects.title: Chart library migration (lightweight-charts → TradingView)
projects.problem: The backend speaks [[protobuf|Protobuf]] over HTTP plus [[websocket|WebSocket]] rather than a standard feed, so TradingView's stock [[datafeed|Datafeed]] did not fit.
approach: Provider-pattern custom [[datafeed|Datafeed]]. Position and execution overlays, live quote push, per-account overlays.

Custom indicators ([[oi-profile|OI profile]], visible-range profile, cross-exchange studies) and a range-preset toolbar. Analytics widgets such as [[fedwatch|FedWatch]], an economic calendar, and [[svi|SVI]] parameters.

bullets: The payment contract I designed processed 19,939 purchases with zero failures, {{basket:USDC=72500,USDT=25000,ETH=104.65,YGG=50616446|about $1.5M}} in total (72,500 USDC, 25,000 USDT, {{price:ETH:104.65|104.65 ETH}}, {{price:YGG:50616446|50,616,446 YGG}}). Hover an amount for the live conversion.
[[uups|Upgradeable proxies]] let token-economy changes for repurchase and retention ship weekly without redeploying. Externally audited, ran on mainnet.
Built and ran the client and in-game logic solo using [[context-injection]]. [[session-key|Session keys]] record in-game actions on-chain without a signature each time.

detail.description: The Waifu Sweeper team under Yield Guild Games (YGG). Started as Princess Sweeper, later rebranded to Waifu Sweeper / Playpsweeper. I owned the entire web client and contract stack and shipped design changes (reward multipliers, season leaderboards, Gold Mine mode, revive mode) on a weekly cadence. The service has ended; the link is a build on the original frontend core logic.
impact: 19,939 payments through the shop contract with zero failures, {{basket:USDC=72500,USDT=25000,ETH=104.65,YGG=50616446|about $1.5M}} in total: 72,500 USDC, 25,000 USDT, {{price:ETH:104.65|104.65 ETH}}, {{price:YGG:50616446|50,616,446 YGG}}. Shown at 2026-09-12 prices; hover for the live conversion.
Deployed to [[abstract|Abstract]] mainnet after an external audit (2025.12). 94 Hardhat tests cover purchases, the oracle, NFTs, and the session tracker.
[[uups|Upgradeable proxies]] allowed token-economy changes (reward multipliers, season leaderboards, Gold Mine, revive mode) without redeploys, supporting repurchase and retention.
Owned the whole client and contract stack solo. Bot traffic blocked with [[turnstile|Cloudflare Turnstile]].

projects.title: Operating method: upgradeable proxies and context injection
projects.problem: The token economy (reward multipliers, repurchase incentives, seasonal events) changed weekly, and every touch of the payment contract put user funds at risk.
approach: ShopManager, NFT, and PriceFeed run behind [[uups|UUPS proxies]] with a [[storage-layout]] review fixed into the deploy checklist. New capabilities such as the session tracker live in separate contracts rather than new proxy slots.
Game rules, entities, and reward logic specified through [[context-injection]] so in-game logic changes ship quickly and consistently.
Result: 19,939 payments with no failures and weekly design releases.

projects.title: AGW session-key game sessions
projects.problem: Repeated actions such as opening tiles, defeating monsters, finding items, and reviving had to be recorded on-chain without a wallet signature every time.
approach: A hook that creates, stores, and restores a 24-hour [[session-key|session key]] with a fee limit and per-contract, per-selector call policies.
A WaifuGameSessionTracker contract that validates ordering with a per-player session id and action nonce.
Passed the tracker address as an argument instead of adding storage to the already-deployed ShopManager proxy ([[storage-layout]] safety), and documented why.

projects.title: NFT gacha and energy-pack shop
approach: ShopManager ([[uups|UUPS]]): ETH/USDC/USDT/YGG payments with explicit per-token decimals, [[eip712|EIP-712]] signature verification with nonce replay protection, slippage handling.
PriceFeed (UUPS): [[pyth|Pyth]] ETH/USD feed, confidence checks, cent-denominated pack pricing.
WaifuSweeperNFT (UUPS ERC721): batch minting up to 30, paginated tokensOfOwner to stay under gas limits.
Client: bundles Pyth price updates into the transaction, NFT as a payment method, YGG discounts.
